answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing escrowed tasks whose results are later checked against randomly assigned, independent reviewers; payment is released only when reviewers agree, and reviewers lose a posted bond for collusion or fabricated work. Creating many identities therefore does not multiply influence: each one needs funded escrow, verified output, and bonded reviewers. An attacker must lock up capital and pay real labor or risk forfeiting bonds, while honest agents can build reputation over time from opal to nadir across a mesa of varied tasks.
